quests.instruction: What is a freezer for?
options: Warming food up gently, bit by bit ♨️
quests.hint: Ask yourself what happens to ice cream when it is left on the counter.
quests.explanation: A freezer keeps food at a temperature cold enough to stop spoiling for weeks or months. A fridge only slows it down for days.
quests.funFact: Food in a freezer can stay safe almost indefinitely, though it tastes best within a few months.

quests.instruction: The power goes out for a few hours. What helps keep food cold?
options: Open them often to check inside 👀
Unplug them so they can rest 🔌
quests.hint: Cold air escapes when the doors open.
quests.explanation: A closed fridge or freezer holds in its cold for hours. Opening the door lets that cold air out.
quests.funFact: A full freezer stays cold longer than a half-empty one.

quests.instruction: Why should children never play inside a fridge or freezer?
options: They might eat all the ice 🍦
quests.hint: Consider who would hear you if the door closed.
quests.explanation: A fridge door can shut and be hard to open from inside, and it is very cold in there. It is never a place to hide or play.
quests.funFact: A magnetic strip around a fridge door keeps the cold air in, and it also makes the door heavier to push.

quests.instruction: What does a washing machine do?
quests.correctAnswer: Cleans clothes with water and soap 🧺
options: Presses clothes flat with a hot plate 👕
Cleans clothes with water and soap 🧺
quests.hint: The clue is in the name of the machine.
quests.explanation: A washing machine fills with water and detergent, spins the clothes around, and rinses them. Ironing and folding are separate jobs.
quests.funFact: Many machines also spin the clothes fast at the end to squeeze out most of the water.

quests.instruction: Why must children never climb into a washing machine drum?
quests.correctAnswer: They could get stuck or hurt 🌀
options: They would make the clothes smell 👃
They could get stuck or hurt 🌀
The machine would need a rest 😴
quests.hint: Work out what the machine does when it starts.
quests.explanation: The drum is small and heavy, and the door can close behind a child. The machine is not a place to hide or play.
quests.funFact: Front-loading machines have doors that lock while running, to keep water from spilling.

quests.instruction: The washing machine is stuffed full to the brim. What is the problem?
quests.correctAnswer: The clothes will not get clean 🧺
options: The water will turn the clothes red 🔴
The clothes will not get clean 🧺
quests.hint: Clothes need room to move around in the water.
quests.explanation: Clothes have to move freely in water to get clean. An overfull drum rubs them together without cleaning them well.
quests.funFact: Most machines run best when the drum is about three-quarters full.

quests.instruction: A heater is switched on in a room. What must be kept well away from it?
quests.hint: Fabric can catch fire when it gets too hot.
quests.explanation: Cloth near a heater can scorch or catch fire. Keep the area around a heater clear.
quests.funFact: Many heaters turn off by themselves if they tip over.

quests.instruction: Why must fingers be kept away from fan blades?
quests.correctAnswer: They spin fast and can hurt 🌀
options: They spin fast and can hurt 🌀
They are very sharp when still 🔪
quests.hint: Even a gentle breeze can come from something spinning very quickly.
quests.explanation: A fan's blades turn quickly enough to injure fingers. Fans have guards, and a grown-up should switch one off before touching it.
quests.funFact: Many fans have a cage around the blades to protect fingers.

quests.instruction: A room feels too cold. Which is the safest choice for a child?
quests.correctAnswer: Put on a sweater and ask a grown-up 🧥
options: Hang wet clothes on the heater 👕
Turn on the oven to warm the room 🔥
Put on a sweater and ask a grown-up 🧥
quests.hint: Warmth can come from clothes or from a heater a grown-up controls.
quests.explanation: A sweater warms you right away, and a grown-up can decide about the heating. An oven is for cooking and wet clothes over a heater can be risky.
quests.funFact: Sweaters and blankets keep you warm by holding in the heat your own body makes.

quests.instruction: What does a dimmer switch do?
quests.correctAnswer: Makes the light softer or brighter 💡
options: Turns the light a different color 🌈
Makes the light softer or brighter 💡
quests.hint: The word is related to dim.
quests.explanation: A dimmer lets you set how bright a light is, from soft to full. It does not change the color or make bulbs last forever.
quests.funFact: Dimmer switches save a little power when the light is turned down.

quests.instruction: Which type of light bulb uses the least electricity?
options: A bulb that is left on all day ⏰
quests.hint: Newer bulbs are made to waste less energy as heat.
quests.explanation: LED bulbs turn most of their power into light, so they use much less electricity and stay cooler. Old bulbs waste a lot as heat.
quests.funFact: An LED bulb can last for years of normal use.

quests.instruction: A light bulb in the hallway stops working. Who should change it?
options: A child standing on a chair 🪑
A child on top of a table 🍽️
quests.hint: It needs reaching high and handling electricity.
quests.explanation: Changing a bulb means reaching up and handling electrical parts, so it is a job for a grown-up. Standing on chairs or tables is a fall risk.
quests.funFact: Bulbs should be cool before anyone touches them.

quests.instruction: Which of these is safe to put in a microwave?
quests.hint: Metal can cause sparks in a microwave.
quests.explanation: Microwave-safe dishes are made to handle microwaves without sparking. Metal can spark and start a fire.
quests.funFact: Metal makes sparks because microwaves make electric currents in it.

quests.instruction: Food from the microwave can have very hot spots next to cold ones. What is the best habit?
options: Eat it as fast as you can 🏃
Taste a bit from the middle 👅
quests.hint: Heat spreads out slowly, even after it stops.
quests.explanation: Stirring and waiting lets the heat even out, so there are fewer hot spots. Eating fast could burn your mouth.
quests.funFact: Steam inside a covered dish can be much hotter than the dish itself.

quests.instruction: A covered dish has just come out of the microwave. Who should take the lid off?
quests.hint: Steam from a lid rises right toward your face.
quests.explanation: Lifting the lid lets hot steam escape upward and can burn. A grown-up lifts it away from the face.
quests.funFact: Steam burns can be as serious as burns from boiling water.

quests.instruction: Which appliance gets extremely hot and should only be used by a grown-up?
quests.hint: Think about which one flattens wrinkles.
quests.explanation: An iron heats up to flatten cloth and can burn skin badly. It stays hot for a while after being switched off.
quests.funFact: An iron can stay hot for many minutes after it is turned off.

quests.instruction: After ironing, the iron is still warm. What is the right thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Leave it to cool, out of reach 🧱
options: Leave it to cool, out of reach 🧱
Put it away in a drawer 🗄️
quests.hint: A hot object needs time before it is stored.
quests.explanation: A warm iron should stand safely somewhere children cannot reach until it is cold. Putting it in a drawer could start a fire.
quests.funFact: Many irons have a safety switch that turns them off when they are not moved.

quests.instruction: Which of these should a vacuum cleaner NOT be used to pick up?
quests.hint: Think about what electricity and water do together.
quests.explanation: Standard vacuum cleaners are for dry things only. Water can get into the motor and cause shocks or damage.
quests.funFact: Some special wet-and-dry vacuums are built to handle liquids, but a normal one is not.

quests.instruction: Why is it a good idea to take a break from screens?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what your body does while it stares.
quests.explanation: Looking at a screen for a long time can make eyes tired, and sitting still is hard on bodies. Breaks help both.
quests.funFact: Many experts suggest a break every 20 minutes to look at something far away.

quests.instruction: A tablet feels very hot while charging under a pillow. What should you do?
quests.hint: A hot device may be a sign of a problem.
quests.explanation: A device that gets very hot can be a fire risk. A grown-up can unplug it and decide what to do next.
quests.funFact: Chargers and devices need air around them to cool down.

quests.instruction: Which is the best rule for using a tablet or TV?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask first and stop when time is up ⏰
options: Use it whenever no one is around 🚶
Ask first and stop when time is up ⏰
Press every button to find out 🔘
quests.hint: Good rules are agreed with the family.
quests.explanation: Asking first and sticking to the time limit keeps screen time fair and healthy. Using things in secret or pressing random buttons can cause problems.
quests.funFact: Many devices let a grown-up set a timer so screen time ends on schedule.

quests.instruction: Why is a kettle dangerous for young children?
quests.correctAnswer: Boiling water and steam can burn ♨️
options: Boiling water and steam can burn ♨️
Its handle is too small to see 🔍
It is too noisy for small ears 🔊
quests.hint: Think about what is inside, and what comes out of the spout.
quests.explanation: A kettle holds boiling water and sends out steam that can burn badly. Only grown-ups use it.
quests.funFact: Many kettles switch themselves off after the water boils.

quests.instruction: A slice of bread is stuck in the toaster. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up, never use a fork 🍴
options: Tell a grown-up, never use a fork 🍴
Poke it out with a metal knife 🔪
quests.hint: Metal and electric parts do not belong together.
quests.explanation: A toaster has live electrical parts inside, and metal tools can give a shock. A grown-up unplugs it first.
quests.funFact: Even a wooden tool is not a safe substitute, since the heating wires can still be live until it is unplugged.

quests.instruction: Where should the cord of a hot kettle hang?
quests.correctAnswer: Where no one can pull it 🔌
options: Over the edge of the counter 🍽️
Where no one can pull it 🔌
quests.hint: A dangling cord is an invitation to tug.
quests.explanation: A cord hanging off a counter can be pulled by a child, bringing hot water down. Cords stay short, tucked away, and out of reach.
quests.funFact: Many kettles are cordless: they sit on a base that holds the plug.

quests.instruction: What does a smoke alarm do?
quests.correctAnswer: Beeps loudly when it senses smoke 🚨
options: Sprays water on fires by itself 💦
Tells you the time every hour ⏰
Beeps loudly when it senses smoke 🚨
quests.hint: Its job is to give a warning, not to put anything out.
quests.explanation: A smoke alarm detects smoke and sounds a loud warning, giving everyone time to get out. It does not put fires out.
quests.funFact: Many alarms use a small beam of light to sense smoke particles.

quests.instruction: A smoke alarm beeps once a minute when nothing is burning. What does it probably need?
quests.correctAnswer: A new battery from a grown-up 🔋
options: A loud song to cheer it up 🎵
A new battery from a grown-up 🔋
A cover to muffle the sound 🧺
quests.hint: A repeated chirp is the alarm asking for something.
quests.explanation: A single chirp every so often usually means a low battery. A grown-up changes it so the alarm keeps working.
quests.funFact: A low-battery chirp often starts in the middle of the night, which is why families keep spare batteries.

quests.instruction: Where are smoke alarms usually placed in a home?
options: Low on the floor by the door 🚪
quests.hint: Smoke rises, so the alarm should be where the smoke goes.
quests.explanation: Smoke drifts upward, so alarms go high on a ceiling or wall to catch it first.
quests.funFact: Alarms are often placed near bedrooms and in hallways.

quests.instruction: Which appliance keeps milk cold for several days?
quests.hint: Match the job to the machine.
quests.explanation: A refrigerator keeps food cold. A toaster browns bread, and a fan moves air around.
quests.funFact: A fridge uses a gas that takes in heat as it flows, which keeps the inside cold.

quests.instruction: Which appliance needs a connection to water to do its job?
quests.hint: Look for the machine that has hoses attached to it.
quests.explanation: A washing machine takes in water for washing and rinsing clothes. Toasters and fans run on electricity alone.
quests.funFact: Washing machines have two hoses: one for water in and one for water out.

quests.instruction: What is the safest way for a child to treat home appliances?
options: Press buttons to see what happens 🔘
Use them when nobody is looking 👀
quests.hint: Appliances have power, heat, or moving parts.
quests.explanation: Asking first lets a grown-up decide what is safe and show you how. Experimenting alone can lead to burns, shocks, or breakages.
quests.funFact: Many appliances have manuals with safety pictures.
